data.name: Banwari
data.gender_notes: Banwari is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who dedicates himself to the worship of Lord Vishnu. Derived from the Sanskrit words 'Ban' (Worship) and 'Vari' (Lord Vishnu). The name Banwari carries the meaning “Worshipper of Lord Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Banwari usually hope their child will grow to embody worshipper of lord vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes devotion and dedication to the divine.
data.etymology: Banwari belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Worshipper of Lord Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Banwari total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Banwari holds a significant place in Hindu culture as it is associated with devotion and selfless service to Lord Vishnu. It carries the legacy of Hindu tradition and values, symbolizing spiritual growth and reverence towards the deity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Banwari holds intrinsic spiritual significance as it represents an individual's commitment towards serving and worshiping Lord Vishnu. This name is believed to be a reminder of the individual's dharma, or duty, to dedicate their time, energy, and resources towards spiritual growth and self-realization. It is a sacred name associated with spiritual purity and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Banwari: The name Banwari symbolizes the one who is filled with joy and bliss, constantly nourishing and purifying the inner self, like a banyan tree providing shelter and strength to all.

historical_references.reference: Banwari was a leader of the Bharat Khandagarh Rajputs, who ruled over the region of Khandesh in present-day Maharashtra, India. He is mentioned in historical texts such as the 'Ain-i-Akbari' and the 'Razia-Nama' and is known to have rebelled against the Mughal Emperor Akbar around 1575.

Banwari was a famous Jain Tirthankara, revered by the Jain community. His life and teachings are detailed in various Jain scriptures. He is believed to have lived around the 5th century BC in the eastern Indian subcontinent.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
